newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Europe's Arianespace upbeat on Ariane-5 '97 tests.
newsitem.headline: Europe's Arianespace upbeat on Ariane-5 '97 tests.

text.p: European satellite launch company Arianespace is confident two test flights scheduled for the Ariane 5 rocket in 1997 would go smoothly, company chief operating officer Francis Avanzi said on Tuesday.

"Sure," Avanzi told Reuters when asked if he was confident the two experimental flights for Ariane 5 in 1997 would be successful after the maiden launch in June ended with ground control blowing up the rocket after it veered off course.
He said an investigation showed the problem was due to "software overflow in the computer" which affected the guidance system.
"It was a small mistake to be corrected," he said.
The rocket was launched from the European Space Agency's launch centre in French Guiana and was blown up just after the 37th second of flight.
Avanzi said Arianespace was able to collect some data during the short flight and had made slight modifications based on the data.

"What we have done is not only to correct this mistake of software but to review all the software, all the interfaces, all the integration in terms of software architecture," said Avanzi, in Singapore for the opening of a regional office.
Arianespace expected full qualification for Ariane 5 by the end of 1997 after the two tests flights, one in the middle of the year and another in the third quarter, he said.
The second test flight in 1997 would carry a commercial satellite, Avanzi said.
He said Arianespace would not make losses with Ariane 5 because of its high reliability as a satellite launcher.
Ariane 5 is able to carry two three-tonne satellites compared to Ariane 4 which can carry a total of 4.8 tonnes.
Company officials told a news conference that Arianespace would use a combination of the two rockets for its satellite launches between 1998 and 2000.

Avanzi told Reuters the company would make 150 million French francs (US$28.8 million) profit in 1996 on revenue of 6.3 billion francs. Profit for 1997 was expected to be around 1996's level on expected sales of nearly 7.0 billion francs.
He said Arianespace was reinvesting more than 3.0 billion francs over the next three years into the year 2000 on Ariane 5.
